study: Abe et al. 2012 (Pacific CHILD, REL Pacific, NCEE 2013-4002)
eval_evidence: Berkeley Policy Associates (BPA), a third-party evaluator with no financial stake, 'worked independently of REL Pacific, the organization that developed and implemented Pacific CHILD'; BPA led the impact study under IES funding.
developer_evidence: REL Pacific staff (the program developers) designed AND implemented/delivered Pacific CHILD to teachers in the three entities; delivery was carried out by REL Pacific program staff, separate from the BPA evaluation team.
cascade_evidence: REL Pacific program staff (developers) delivered the annual institute, mini-institutes, lesson demonstrations and classroom observations directly to the grade 4-5 teachers; no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools received business-as-usual reading instruction; comparison/control = business-as-usual per design and extraction record.
coaching_evidence: Beyond the annual institute/mini-institutes, the model includes monthly lesson demonstrations, twice-monthly in-class classroom observations, and weekly structured learning team meetings in teachers' own schools/classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Pure teacher PD; only the teachers' own grade 4-5 reading-comprehension instruction changes. No tutoring, pull-out, or added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Pacific CHILD is a designed two-year intervention; outcomes measured at end of Year 2 for the single cohort of teachers new to the program (its first rollout in these schools, no prior implementation year).
